d: The NDPA 2023 obligation to notify the NDPC within 72 hours of becoming aware of a personal data breach likely to result in risk to data subjects’ rights.
Accounting and Auditing Organisation for Islamic Financial Institutions; the primary global standard-setter for Shari’ah compliance in Takaful and Islamic finance.
The insurer’s decision to provide coverage, either at standard rates or with a rating or exclusion.
A group life rider paying an additional benefit if death is caused by an accident.
The period during which an RSA holder or pension plan participant makes contributions and builds up their retirement fund.

t: ACIIN (Associate of the Chartered Insurance Institute of Nigeria)
d: The Associateship qualification; a higher professional designation required for key management roles under NIIRA 2025.
The insurer’s formal confirmation of receipt of a claim notification, required under NIIRA 2025 within 5 business days.
A numerical estimate of a future experience factor (mortality rate, interest rate, lapse rate, expense level) used in life insurance pricing and reserving.
The certification issued by the Statutory Actuary confirming the adequacy of the insurer’s technical provisions, filed with NAICOM annually.
The annual review by the Statutory Actuary of the insurer’s life business, confirming reserve adequacy and the financial condition of the portfolio.
The risk that an insurer’s actual claims experience will differ from the mortality, morbidity, or other statistical assumptions used in product pricing and reserving.

A professional trained in the mathematics and statistics of financial risk, specialising in the long-term financial implications of uncertain events. In life insurance, the actuary is responsible for pricing, reserving, capital assessment, and regulatory reporting.
Assets that qualify for inclusion in the insurer’s solvency margin calculation under NAICOM’s admissible asset framework.

The tendency for individuals with higher-than-average risk to disproportionately seek insurance, because they know their risk level exceeds what the insurer has priced for. Managed through underwriting and group enrolment controls.

The continent-wide free trade agreement creating a single market for goods and services across 54 African Union member states; creating potential for cross-border insurance market development, reinsurance capacity pooling, and regulatory harmonisation.
A sworn written statement used as evidence in legal and claims proceedings.

A defined population sharing a common characteristic or institutional membership to whom insurance is offered at group rates or with simplified underwriting, using the institutional relationship as a distribution and trust pathway.
The pan-African reinsurer owned by African Union member states; a major domestic reinsurance capacity provider for Nigerian cedants.
The total first-year premium from new policies written in a period, annualised to a 12-month basis regardless of the premium frequency.
The collective body of tied agents appointed by an insurer to sell its products.
The management structure of a retail agency force, defining roles, spans of control, and reporting lines from individual agents through unit managers and branch managers to the agency director.
An individual licensed by NAICOM to sell insurance products on behalf of one or more licensed insurers.
The simulation of human intelligence by computer systems; applied in insurance for underwriting, fraud detection, and claims processing.
A Yoruba term for a traditional rotating savings and credit association (ROSCA); a community-based informal savings mechanism that competes with insurance as a financial protection tool.

Traditional Nigerian rotating savings groups in which members contribute at regular intervals and each member receives the pool in rotation. A powerful entry point for community-level insurance marketing.

An insurance delivery model integrated with traditional Nigerian rotating savings groups, in which an insurance premium component is added to the regular group contribution and collected collectively by the group leader.
The committee responsible for oversight of the insurer’s ALM strategy, typically comprising the CEO, CFO, CIO, and Statutory Actuary.
The governance body responsible for overseeing the investment function and ensuring the investment strategy remains consistent with the liability profile. Required by NIIRA 2025.
A contract whose financial outcome depends on an uncertain event; insurance is the classic aleatory contract because the premium is certain but the benefit is conditional on a covered event.
A defined set of rules or instructions for solving a problem or making a decision; used in automated underwriting and risk scoring.
Data generated by digital behaviour (mobile money transactions, airtime usage, geolocation) used to supplement traditional underwriting data.

Non-traditional data sources (mobile money transactions, airtime behaviour, BVN data, geolocation) used in AI-powered underwriting as predictors of mortality risk in addition to traditional medical and demographic data.

Anti-Money Laundering and Countering the Financing of Terrorism; the regulatory framework requiring insurers to implement KYC, transaction monitoring, and suspicious activity reporting under the MLPPA 2022.
An examination command word requiring the candidate to break a concept or situation into its components and examine each in detail.
The annual percentage of fund value deducted from a unit-linked policy to cover investment management and administration costs.
The standard metric for measuring new business production, expressing the first-year premium on each policy in annual terms (monthly premium × 12).
The person receiving income payments under a life annuity.
A contract under which an insurer pays a periodic income to the annuitant for life (or a defined period) in exchange for a lump sum at the outset. See Retirement Life Annuity.
The monthly income payable per unit of purchase price; the primary metric for comparing annuity quotations.
The regulatory framework and operational practices designed to prevent insurance products from being used to launder proceeds of crime or finance terrorism.

The tendency for individuals with higher-than-average mortality risk to disproportionately seek insurance, or to seek larger amounts of it, relative to low-risk individuals. Underwriting is the primary mechanism for managing anti-selection.
A set of protocols enabling two software systems to communicate and exchange data; the technical foundation of embedded insurance integration.
Investment instruments specifically approved by NAICOM for inclusion in an insurer’s solvency margin calculation.

The broad field of computer science aimed at building systems that perform tasks requiring human-like intelligence: pattern recognition, language understanding, and learning from experience. In insurance, typically refers to machine learning applications.
An examination command word requiring the candidate to evaluate the value, importance, or implications of a topic.
A professional appointed by the insurer to investigate and evaluate the circumstances and value of a claim.
The division of an investment portfolio among different asset classes (equities, bonds, real estate, money market) in defined proportions.
The management of assets and liabilities together to minimise the risk of a financial mismatch; particularly important for annuity and long-term life business.
The transfer of a policyholder’s rights under an insurance policy to another party; must comply with the terms of the policy and the Insurance Act.
The transfer of a policyholder’s rights under an insurance policy to another party, subject to the insurer’s acceptance.

t: Associate of the Chartered Insurance Institute of Nigeria (ACIIN)
d: The Associateship qualification required of key management officers including Heads of Underwriting, Claims, and Financial Planning under NIIRA 2025.
The person on whose life the insurance is effected; the insured. May or may not be the same as the policyholder.
The index value at which a parametric insurance policy begins to pay. Below the attachment point, no benefit is payable regardless of the insured’s actual loss.

A structured report completed by the applicant’s treating doctor at the insurer’s request, providing clinical detail on a disclosed condition. The most informative third-party medical evidence tool in life underwriting.
The clause in a will certifying that the will was properly signed and witnessed.
The Board committee responsible for overseeing the integrity of financial statements and the internal and external audit functions.
A rules-based or AI-powered system making underwriting decisions without human intervention for standard risk applications.
See Free Cover Limit.
The maximum sum assured the reinsurer will automatically accept under the treaty without individual case review. Risks above the ABL require facultative placement.
A reinsurance agreement under which the cedant is obligated to cede, and the reinsurer is obligated to accept, all business meeting defined criteria, without case-by-case facultative placement.
An additional premium charged for coverage of the risk of death in aviation accidents.
The proportion of the Nigerian population that lacks knowledge of what insurance is, what it covers, how much it costs, or how to access it.
Relevant in military and paramilitary group life claims; a risk that unconfirmed deaths may be claimed while the individual is absent without leave rather than deceased.
A strategic performance measurement framework translating strategy into objectives across financial, customer, process, and learning perspectives.
A strategic performance measurement framework translating strategy into measurable objectives across four perspectives: financial, customer, internal process, and learning and growth.
The distribution of insurance products through a bank’s existing customer network and branch infrastructure.
The insurer’s representative embedded at a bank branch level to support bancassurance product sales, training, and compliance. Reports to the Bancassurance Manager.

The risk that an index-based insurance product’s trigger index does not perfectly correlate with the individual insured’s actual loss experience. A farmer whose crop fails due to local conditions may not receive a payment if the official index does not record a triggering event.
Direct, targeted, non-mass-media marketing activities including branch activation, community events, religious community partnerships, and Ajo/Esusu group integration.
The person or entity designated to receive the death benefit under a life insurance policy.
The policyholder’s formal designation of who will receive the death benefit.
The designation by a policyholder of the person(s) entitled to receive the death benefit, enabling direct payment to the nominee without passing through the insured’s estate.
The amount payable by the insurer to the beneficiary or policyholder upon the occurrence of a covered event.
The PAS module computing policy values: surrender value, paid-up value, death benefit (including bonuses for participating policies), and maturity benefit.
The actuarial reserve representing the present value of future benefits less the present value of future premiums; the insurer’s obligation to fund future benefit payments.
The document listing the covered services and their limits in a health insurance plan.
Very large datasets requiring specialised tools to process and analyse; used in insurance for risk pricing, fraud detection, and customer analytics.
Authority granted to a coverholder or managing agent to enter into insurance contracts on behalf of the insurer.
A distributed, tamper-evident ledger maintained by multiple network participants; used in parametric insurance and reinsurance settlement.
A premium loading applied where an applicant’s blood pressure readings indicate elevated cardiovascular mortality risk.
A measure of body weight relative to height used in medical underwriting to assess obesity-related mortality risk.
The foundational governance document defining the Board’s role, composition, authority, and relationship with management.

The apex governance body of a Nigerian life insurance company, accountable to shareholders for the oversight of strategy, risk management, financial performance, and regulatory compliance; composed under NIIRA 2025 requirements for a majority of non-executive directors and minimum independent directors.
A court order by a Beneficiary of Interests; may affect the distribution of a death benefit where the policyholder’s estate is involved.
The weighted average time to receipt of bond cash flows; the primary measure of the bond’s price sensitivity to interest rate changes.
A guaranteed addition to the sum assured of a with-profits policy, declared annually and once added cannot be removed.
An additional bonus payable at maturity or earlier death on a with-profits policy, in addition to the accumulated reversionary bonuses.
An automated conversational programme; used in insurance for first-level customer service, claims notification, and policy queries.
A market sizing approach that builds the estimate from granular data about specific employer groups, geographic areas, or product segments.

The ongoing measurement of brand awareness, brand perception, and net promoter score through consumer surveys and social listening, used to assess the impact of marketing investment on brand strength.
The deliberate process of establishing a specific, distinct, and credible place for the insurer’s brand in the consumer’s mind, relative to competitors and the consumer’s own values.
An intermediary who acts on behalf of the client (not the insurer) to source and place insurance coverage, regulated under NIIRA 2025.
The commission earned by a broker for placing insurance on behalf of a client; distinct from agent commission in that it is paid to an intermediary acting for the buyer.
The remuneration paid by the insurer to the broker as a percentage of the gross premium on each policy placed. The primary revenue source for most Nigerian brokers.
The three technology sourcing options: building capability internally, purchasing a commercial platform, or collaborating with an Insurtech or fintech partner that brings the capability.
A transaction in which a defined benefit pension scheme transfers its pension payment obligations to a life insurer.
The process of ensuring critical business operations can continue or be rapidly restored following a major disruption, governed by a Board-approved BCM plan tested at least annually.
The component of BCM that assesses the impact of disruption to each critical business process, including the Maximum Tolerable Period of Disruption and the Minimum Business Continuity Objective.

A legal contract between business partners specifying the terms under which a deceased or disabled partner’s business interest is transferred to the surviving partners, typically funded by cross-purchase or entity-purchase life insurance.
The total cost incurred to acquire one new policyholder, including marketing, agent commission, and underwriting costs.
A process in which managers review each other’s proposed performance ratings to ensure consistency across the team, preventing rating inflation or compression.
Companies and Allied Matters Act 2020; the primary corporate governance legislation for Nigerian companies.
The maximum amount of risk a reinsurer (or insurer) is willing and able to accept.
The legal ability of a person to enter into an insurance contract; minors may not enter into insurance contracts in their own right.
The requirement that an insurer hold sufficient capital (assets in excess of liabilities) to absorb unexpected losses and protect policyholders.
A payment model in which the HMO pays providers a fixed amount per enrolled member per month regardless of services utilised.
An examination question presenting a real or hypothetical business scenario, requiring application of knowledge to the specific facts given.
An ALM approach in which the specific cash flows generated by assets on specific dates are structured to exactly match the specific liability cash flows due on those dates.
A reinsurance cover responding when aggregate claims from a single catastrophic event exceed a defined retention.
The risk of an extreme event generating losses many multiples above normal expectations (pandemic, earthquake, workplace disaster).
Latin for ‘let the buyer beware’. Less applicable in insurance than in commercial contracts due to the insurer’s duty to explain policy terms clearly under NIIRA 2025.
The apex bank regulator; relevant to insurance for bancassurance regulatory coordination and financial system stability.

The joint guidelines issued by the Central Bank of Nigeria and NAICOM governing bancassurance arrangements in Nigeria, addressing permitted models, product restrictions, staff licensing, premium remittance, and consumer protection.
The insurer that cedes (transfers) risk to a reinsurer.
A payment by the reinsurer to the cedant under a proportional treaty (particularly co-insurance), representing a reimbursement of the cedant’s initial acquisition costs on the ceded business.
The full schedule of all eligible employees in a group life scheme, containing age, gender, occupation, salary, and sum assured data.
See MD/CEO.
A document certifying that an insurance policy is in force, typically issued to third parties as evidence of coverage.
The portion of risk (and corresponding premium) transferred from the cedant to the reinsurer.
The senior executive responsible for financial management, reporting, investment, and NAICOM statutory filing.
The strategic allocation of distribution resources across multiple channels to maximise premium income, control cost, manage compliance risk, and serve diverse customer segments effectively.

A software programme engaging in automated text-based conversations with users, answering predefined questions and completing defined tasks; deployed in insurance for policy status queries, claims notification, and basic servicing.

The senior executive responsible for the insurer’s regulatory compliance programme, AML/KYC obligations, NDPA 2023 compliance, and the management of the regulatory relationship with NAICOM and other regulators.
The executive responsible for the ERM framework, risk monitoring, ORSA, and independent risk oversight. Required for Nigerian life insurers above defined thresholds under NIIRA 2025.
A life assurance policy taken out on the life of a child, typically to build savings for education or other milestones.
The professional body for insurance practitioners in Nigeria, conducting examinations, awarding qualifications, and setting CPD standards.
The Chartered Insurance Institute of Nigeria’s flagship professional development event; generates CPD credit hours.
The CIIN Certificate of Proficiency; the minimum licensing qualification for insurance agents under NIIRA 2025.

The minimum professional qualification required under NIIRA 2025 for all individuals who sell, solicit, or negotiate life insurance products in Nigeria; obtained through CIIN examinations covering insurance principles, life products, and insurance law.

The professional standards document published by the Chartered Insurance Institute of Nigeria that establishes the ethical obligations of all CIIN members, covering integrity, competence, duty to the client, fair dealing, regulatory compliance, and confidentiality.
A scheduled sitting of CIIN examinations; typically held at least twice per year.
Three levels: Foundation (Certificate of Proficiency and Cert. CIIN); Diploma (Dip. CIIN); Associateship (ACIIN) and Fellowship (FCIIN).
A formal request by a policyholder or beneficiary for payment of a benefit under an insurance policy.
The standardised document completed by a claimant to initiate an insurance claim.
The person making a claim; may be the policyholder, beneficiary, or legal representative.
The complete process of receiving, assessing, approving, and settling insurance claims.

The broker’s role in assisting and representing the client throughout the insurance claims process, including documentation preparation, insurer liaison, dispute escalation, and settlement negotiation.
A cultural pathology in which claims staff are evaluated on claims costs minimised rather than claims fairly settled, resulting in delayed and disputed claims and industry-wide reputational damage.
The deliberate submission of a false or inflated claim to obtain an insurance benefit to which the claimant is not entitled.
An actuarial reserve representing estimated claims that have occurred but have not yet been notified to the insurer.
Total claims incurred as a percentage of total premium earned; primary health insurance performance measure.
Total health claims incurred as a percentage of total premium earned; the primary health insurance performance metric.
The operational function responsible for receiving, assessing, investigating, and settling claims made by or on behalf of policyholders under the terms of their life assurance policies.

The PAS module managing the end-to-end claims workflow from notification to settlement, with automated SLA monitoring against the 60-day statutory settlement requirement (NIIRA 2025 s.210) and the insurer’s 5-day acknowledgement standard.
Funds held by the insurer to pay claims that have been notified but not yet settled, and claims estimated to be incurred but not yet reported.
The period from receipt of complete claims documentation to payment of the benefit; NIIRA 2025 mandates maximum settlement times.
A PII policy that responds to claims made during the policy period, regardless of when the alleged negligence occurred, provided it was after the retroactive date.
A defined category of insurance business (life, non-life, composite) for which a separate NAICOM licence is required.
An application that presents no adverse risk factors and is accepted at standard premium rates without any loading or exclusion.

The risk that climate change affects the insurer’s portfolio through physical mortality effects, morbidity impacts (disease expansion, heat-related illness), lapse rate increases in climate-affected regions, and investment portfolio devaluation of climate-vulnerable assets.
A premium loading applied in individual underwriting based on a specific medical condition or clinical finding.
The delivery of computing services (servers, storage, databases, software) over the internet; enabling more scalable and cost-efficient technology infrastructure for insurers.
The sharing of a single large risk among multiple insurers, each accepting a defined percentage of the total coverage. Used for risks that exceed a single insurer’s capacity.
A life reinsurance method in which the reinsurer assumes a proportionate share of the full policy economics, premium, reserve, and benefits. The reinsurer holds its share of the policy reserve.
The fixed amount paid by the insured at the point of service, shared with the insurer as a moral hazard management tool.
The behavioural standards document for directors, executives, and employees.
An addition or amendment to a will; relevant in life insurance claims where the beneficiary designation in the will differs from the policy nomination.
Unsolicited contact with prospective customers; regulated under NIIRA 2025 and NDPA 2023 to protect consumers from aggressive marketing.
An ML recommendation technique that identifies patterns across similar users (‘customers with your profile also purchased these products’); used in insurance product recommendation engines.
The Nigerian Code of Corporate Governance 2018 issued by the FRC, setting governance standards for public interest entities including listed insurers.
The date on which an insurance policy becomes effective.
Remuneration paid by the insurer to an agent or broker for placing insurance business.
The recovery by the insurer of first-year commission from an agent when a policy lapses within a defined early period.

Insurance organised around existing social structures (cooperatives, market associations, Ajo/Esusu groups, religious communities) using the community’s trust network and collective meeting structure for distribution, premium collection, and claims advocacy.
The termination of a reinsurance treaty, typically involving a lump-sum payment to settle all outstanding obligations.
The primary Nigerian corporate law, governing company formation, directors’ duties, and annual reporting requirements for all registered companies.
An examination command word requiring identification of similarities and differences between two or more items.
Systematic monitoring and analysis of competitor products, pricing, distribution investments, and financial performance to inform strategic positioning decisions.
The systematic gathering, analysis, and distribution of information about the competitive, regulatory, and market environment to support strategic decision-making.
A company licensed for both standard insurance and microinsurance, maintaining the microinsurance book as a separately identified fund within the composite operation.

Insurance that specific categories of persons or entities are legally required to hold: Third Party Motor Insurance, Employer’s Group Life, Occupiers’ Liability, Builders’ Liability, Aviation Third Party Liability, and Credit Life for qualifying loans.
The deliberate withholding of material facts from the insurer at the time of application. A form of non-disclosure that may entitle the insurer to void the policy.
The risk of excessive exposure to a single counterparty, asset class, geographic area, or product line.
The terms and obligations in an insurance policy that must be met by the policyholder to maintain coverage.
A medical report obtained from the applicant’s own doctor, providing the insurer with additional health information.
The document defining conflicts of interest, disclosure obligations, and recusal processes.
The consistent application of appropriate consequences for conduct violations.
The process of preventing policy lapses through proactive outreach to at-risk policyholders.

A structured set of interventions designed to retain policyholders who are considering or have initiated a surrender or cancellation, by presenting alternatives and ensuring the customer has full information to make a genuinely informed decision.
In insurance contract law, the premium paid by the policyholder in exchange for the insurer’s promise of indemnity or benefit.
A deep understanding of consumer behaviour, attitudes, barriers, and motivations, derived from structured market research, that informs product development, marketing, and strategy.
The regulatory framework protecting policyholders from unfair practices by insurers and intermediaries.
The NAICOM division responsible for handling policyholder complaints, monitoring market conduct, and enforcing the consumer protection provisions of NIIRA 2025.
The risk that difficulties in one institution or market spread to others, including the insurer’s own operations.
The creation and distribution of educational or informative content that builds the insurer’s authority and trust, without directly selling a product in every piece of content.
The period (typically the first 1–2 years of a policy) during which the insurer may investigate and potentially deny a claim based on material misrepresentation.
A claim that the insurer disputes on grounds of non-disclosure, exclusion applicability, or lack of evidence.
A major Nigerian-based pan-African reinsurer providing proportional and non-proportional reinsurance capacity to Nigerian cedants.
A pan-African private-sector reinsurer headquartered in Lagos. The leading private domestic reinsurer in Nigeria, with operations across multiple African markets.

Additional remuneration paid by an insurer to a broker based on the volume or profitability of business placed with that insurer. Must be disclosed to clients under NIIRA 2025 and the NCRIB Code of Ethics.

The systematic maintenance, improvement, and broadening of skills and knowledge throughout a professional career; CIIN members must complete a defined number of CPD hours annually as a condition of membership renewal.
A legal doctrine requiring ambiguous insurance policy terms to be interpreted against the party that drafted them (the insurer).

An insurance contract that compensates the insured for the actual financial loss suffered, up to the policy limit. Life insurance is generally not an indemnity contract; it pays a fixed sum regardless of actual financial loss.
Under IFRS 17, the deferred profit element of a life insurance contract liability, released into income progressively over the coverage period as insurance services are provided.

The principle under which, where more than one insurance policy covers the same risk, each insurer contributes proportionally to the total loss. More relevant to general insurance; modified in the life insurance context.
Nigeria’s mandatory defined-contribution pension system, established under the Pension Reform Act 2004 and reformed in 2014.
A senior management or governance role in a licensed insurer that carries material responsibility and is therefore subject to NAICOM’s fit and proper assessment before appointment.
The proportion of leads or prospects that result in issued policies; a key digital channel distribution metric.
A term assurance that includes the right to convert to a whole life or endowment policy without further medical evidence at a defined future date.
A member-owned organisation providing savings, credit, and mutual support; a major community distribution channel for microinsurance and informal sector financial services.
A company licensed to distribute insurance products on behalf of a licensed insurer; includes banks (bancassurance), fintech companies, and other platform businesses.
A fixed-income security issued by a corporation, offering higher yield than government bonds but with credit risk.
A comprehensive package of insurance and savings products provided by an employer to its employees, including group life, health, and pension.
The system of structures, processes, rules, and practices by which a company is directed and controlled, ensuring accountability to shareholders, policyholders, regulators, and the broader public.

The Enterprise Risk Management framework published by the Committee of Sponsoring Organizations of the Treadway Commission. Explicitly integrates risk management with strategic planning and performance management.
A competitive strategy based on having the lowest cost base in the market, enabling competitive pricing and superior margins at market-rate premiums.
The insurer’s offer to cover a risk on terms different from those applied for; requires the proposer’s acceptance to form a contract.
Total admissible assets as a percentage of total life insurance liabilities. NAICOM requires this ratio to be maintained above 100% at all times.
The systematic maintenance of professional knowledge and skills throughout a career.
The statistical weight given to an insurer’s own experience data in experience rating, reflecting the volume and reliability of that data.
Life insurance covering the outstanding balance of a loan in the event of the borrower’s death or total permanent disability, with the lender as beneficiary.
An independent assessment of the creditworthiness of a bond issuer or debt instrument, expressed as a letter grade (e.g., AAA, AA, B).
The risk of loss arising from the failure of a counterparty (bond issuer, bank, reinsurer) to meet its financial obligations.

A lump-sum benefit payable upon the diagnosis of a specified dread disease (such as cancer, myocardial infarction, or stroke) that meets the policy’s clinical definition, provided the policyholder survives the survival period.
A group life or standalone rider paying a lump sum on diagnosis of a defined critical illness.
Insurance paying a lump sum on diagnosis of a specified serious medical condition, provided the insured survives the survival period.
An examination command word at Associateship level requiring a balanced, evidence-based assessment of a proposition, including arguments for and against.
A digital platform used by agents and sales managers to manage prospect pipelines, record client interactions, track policy portfolios, and set persistency alert follow-ups.

Software managing interactions with prospects and policyholders: contact details, interaction history, pipeline status, and activity records. The bridge between the agent’s sales activity and the PAS policy records.
The senior executive responsible for the ERM framework, ORSA, and monitoring material risks, with direct Board access.

A buy-sell funding arrangement in which each business partner purchases a life insurance policy on the other partners; on death, the surviving partners use the proceeds to buy out the deceased partner’s share from their estate.
Offering additional insurance products to existing policyholders based on their profile and existing coverage.
Marketing communications that use culturally familiar concepts, language, metaphors, and values to make the message more relatable and persuasive to the target audience.
The risk of financial loss arising from adverse movements in exchange rates between the Naira and foreign currencies in which the insurer holds assets.
The total cost to acquire a new policyholder, including digital marketing, platform costs, and any commission paid to digital partners.

A metric measuring how easy it was for a customer to complete an interaction, rated on a scale from ‘strongly disagree’ to ‘strongly agree’ with the statement ‘the company made it easy to handle my issue.’

Every interaction a policyholder has with an insurer across the full relationship lifecycle (from awareness through purchase, in-force servicing, and claims) and the cumulative impression those interactions create.

A structured representation of every significant interaction a customer has with the insurer, documenting the customer’s goals, emotional state, pain points, and the insurer’s moments of truth at each stage.
A transaction-level metric measuring customer satisfaction with a specific interaction, typically on a 1–5 or 1–10 scale administered immediately after the interaction.

Insurance products covering losses arising from cybercrime, data breaches, ransomware, and business interruption caused by cyber events; covering both first-party (direct losses to the insured) and third-party (liability to affected customers and regulators) exposures.
The practice of protecting computer systems and data from unauthorised access, theft, and disruption.
The risk of unauthorised access to the insurer’s systems, data exfiltration, ransomware, or service disruption.
The Islamic doctrine of necessity, permitting an otherwise prohibited action when no permissible alternative is available; applied in Takaful where no re-Takaful capacity exists.
The systematic analysis of data to identify patterns, draw conclusions, and support decision-making.

A category of data controller under the NDPA 2023, including life insurance companies, that is subject to enhanced compliance obligations: mandatory NDPC registration, Data Protection Officer appointment, and Data Protection Impact Assessments.

A classification under NDPA 2023 for organisations that process personal data at scale or process special category data, triggering the highest tier of compliance obligations including mandatory DPO, DPCP, and biennial audit.
The framework of policies, processes, and accountability for managing data assets in compliance with NDPA 2023 and other requirements.
The NDPA 2023 / GAID 2025 requirement that personal data of Nigerian data subjects be stored primarily on servers physically located in Nigeria; material to cloud deployment decisions.
The annual compliance programme document submitted by DCPMIs to the NDPC, describing the organisation’s data governance framework, processing activities, and compliance measures.
A mandatory assessment before commencing high-risk processing activities, evaluating the nature and necessity of the processing, risks to data subjects, and required mitigation measures.

A mandatory appointee for DCPMIs responsible for overseeing data protection compliance, advising on processing activities, cooperating with the NDPC, and acting as the contact point for data subject rights.
A request by a data subject for a copy of all personal data held about them, together with information on processing purposes, legal bases, and third parties; must be responded to within 30 days.
See Grace Period.
An official document issued by the appropriate civil authority certifying the date, location, and cause of death; primary evidence in death claims.
The insurer’s refusal to provide coverage, typically because the risk is too high or falls outside the insurer’s appetite.
Term assurance where the sum assured reduces over the policy term, typically used to cover a repayment mortgage.
The retirement period during which accumulated pension savings are converted into income, either through a Retirement Life Annuity or Programmed Withdrawal.
The amount the insured must pay out-of-pocket before the insurer covers remaining costs; more common in indemnity plans.

A subset of ML using multi-layered neural networks to learn representations of complex, high-dimensional data (text, images, audio). Requires very large datasets; most relevant insurance application is NLP.
The risk that a bond issuer fails to make the scheduled interest or principal payment.
A life annuity in which contributions are made during an accumulation phase with income commencing at a future date.
An examination command word requiring a precise, concise statement of the meaning of a term.
A pension arrangement in which the employer promises a defined retirement benefit based on salary and years of service.
A pension arrangement in which contributions are defined but the retirement benefit depends on accumulated fund performance; the CPS is a DC scheme.
The document mapping financial and operational approval authority from Board to individual managers.
A family member (spouse, child) covered under an employee’s health insurance plan.
An examination command word requiring a detailed account of a concept, process, or product.
A competitive strategy based on offering products or services that customers recognise as distinctively superior to alternatives and are willing to pay a premium for.
A company holding a NAICOM corporate agent licence that distributes insurance through a digital platform.
The use of digital channels (mobile app, USSD, website, embedded API) as the primary or supplementary mechanism for reaching insurance customers.
See Full-Stack Digital Insurer.
The completion of the insurance application, underwriting, and policy issuance workflow digitally, without paper documents, using e-forms, identity verification, and electronic signature.

A business strategy that uses technology as its primary enabler, defining how digital tools will transform customer acquisition, policyholder servicing, risk assessment, and claims management to improve competitive position.
The intermediate CIIN qualification, covering underwriting, claims, reinsurance, distribution, and risk management.
Insurance sold directly by the insurer to the customer without an intermediary, typically through advertising, mail, telephone, or digital channels.
Insurance providing periodic income replacement if the insured becomes unable to work due to illness or injury. Also called income protection insurance.
The obligation of the proposer to reveal all material facts to the insurer at the time of application.
An examination command word requiring a balanced consideration of multiple aspects of a topic.
A structured intervention managing enrollees with chronic conditions to prevent expensive acute events and reduce claims costs.
The production by an AI model of systematically different outcomes for different demographic groups without actuarial justification; a fairness violation under NAICOM’s TCF framework.
An examination command word requiring identification of the differences between two or more terms or concepts.
The mechanism through which insurance products are sold to customers: tied agent, bancassurance, broker, direct, digital, embedded.
A distribution of profits by a company to its shareholders; a component of equity investment return.
The regulatory requirement for Nigerian insurers to offer a defined proportion of their reinsurance to Nigerian domestic reinsurers before placing internationally.

The regulatory requirement under Nigerian insurance law for direct insurers to offer a defined minimum proportion of all reinsurance placements to domestic reinsurers before accessing international capacity.
The obligation of Nigerian insurers under NIIRA 2025 to offer a defined proportion of their reinsurance to domestic reinsurers before placing with international markets.
The weighted average time to receipt of cash flows from a bond or portfolio; the primary measure of interest rate sensitivity.
A measure of a bond or portfolio’s sensitivity to interest rate changes, expressed as the approximate percentage price change for a 1% change in interest rates.
The difference between the duration of the insurer’s assets and the duration of its liabilities; a positive gap means assets are shorter-dated than liabilities, creating reinvestment risk.

The legal obligation to exercise the standard of care that a reasonably competent professional in the relevant role would exercise, such that the customer does not suffer harm from the practitioner’s negligence.

The obligation of the proposer to disclose all material facts that would influence a prudent insurer in deciding whether to accept the risk and at what terms. Governed by the Insurance Act and modified by NIIRA 2025 to impose a reciprocal duty on insurers.
A life table function: the number of lives dying between exact ages x and x+1. dx = lx − lx+1.
A legally recognised digital alternative to a wet signature; valid for insurance contracts under the Evidence Act 2011 provided the signature is verifiably linked to the signatory’s identity.

A savings-plus-protection product specifically designed for education funding, maturing at the projected date of the child’s school enrolment and providing the full maturity benefit immediately if the parent dies or is permanently disabled before maturity.

The set of investment portfolios that maximise expected return for a given level of risk, or minimise risk for a given expected return. The optimal portfolio lies on the efficient frontier, subject to regulatory and ALM constraints.
Enhancing Financial Innovation and Access; the primary source of demand-side data on financial inclusion and insurance in Nigeria.
The organisation conducting the biennial Access to Financial Services in Nigeria survey, the primary demand-side data source for Nigerian insurance market research.

The standard actuarial mortality table for Nigerian life insurance practice, derived from the experience of Nigerian insured lives. Provides age- and sex-specific qx values for individual pricing and reserving.
The Nigerian mortality tables (Experience Follows Up life tables) published for use in life insurance underwriting and pricing.
Insurance integrated into a non-insurance product or transaction, automatically activated at the point of the primary transaction.
The present value of shareholders’ interest in a life insurance company: Adjusted Net Asset Value (ANAV) plus Value of In-Force Business (VIF).
A specialist sales executive who manages the insurer’s corporate relationships with employers, selling group life schemes, worksite products, and pension-linked benefits to HR directors and CFOs.
The highest-value form of group life broking, in which the broker advises employers on the full design, management, and communication of integrated employee benefit programmes.
The total package offered by an employer to attract and retain employees, including insurance and pension benefits.
Group life insurance provided by an employer to its employees; mandatory under the Pension Reform Act 2014 at a minimum of 3× annual emoluments.
A written amendment to an insurance policy, modifying the original terms.
A life insurance policy that pays the sum assured on death within the term or on survival to the maturity date, combining protection with savings.
A life annuity paying higher-than-standard income to an annuitant with a diagnosed medical condition reducing life expectancy.
A more intensive level of KYC and AML assessment applied to higher-risk customers: PEPs, high-premium transactions, customers from high-risk jurisdictions, or unusual transaction patterns.
The systematic, organisation-wide process of identifying, assessing, and managing all risks faced by an insurer, integrated with strategy and capital management, and subject to Board governance.
The actuarial principle that the expected present value of premiums received must equal the expected present value of benefits paid. This principle determines the net premium.
A structured, comprehensive approach to identifying, assessing, managing, monitoring, and reporting all material risks across an organisation.
A life annuity that increases at a defined rate each year to preserve real purchasing power.

An investment approach incorporating Environmental, Social, and Governance factors alongside financial return metrics; for Nigerian insurers, applied through FGN Green Sukuk, infrastructure bond ESG screening, and equity exclusion screens.
A long-form examination question requiring a structured, discursive response at Associateship level.

A life insurance strategy used when a testator wishes to leave equal inheritance to multiple children but their assets cannot easily be divided, with the life insurance providing a balancing cash payment to children who do not receive the indivisible asset.

The process of arranging the management and distribution of one’s assets during life and at death in accordance with one’s intentions, using wills, trusts, beneficiary nominations, and life insurance to protect dependants and manage the tax and administrative consequences of death.
An Igbo term for a traditional rotating savings and credit association; equivalent to Ajo.
See Critically Evaluate.
The total package of benefits and experiences offered to employees to attract and retain them.
A payment made by the insurer as a goodwill gesture without admission of legal liability; used in borderline claims or to resolve disputes.
A non-proportional reinsurance arrangement under which the reinsurer pays claims (or aggregate claims) exceeding a defined priority level, up to a maximum. Structured per-life or in aggregate.
A non-proportional reinsurance arrangement under which the reinsurer pays the portion of a loss exceeding the cedant’s retention.

A specific condition, circumstance, or cause of loss that is not covered under the policy. An exclusion may be used instead of a decline where the risk is otherwise acceptable but one element is uninsurable.
Conditions or circumstances not covered under a health insurance plan.
A policy provision specifying circumstances or risks that are not covered.
The primary management decision-making forum chaired by the MD/CEO.
An insurance-backed executive pension plan in which the employer purchases a policy on the executive’s life as deferred compensation.
An employer-sponsored supplementary pension arrangement for senior executives, bridging the gap between CPS-generated and target retirement income.
The amount added to the net premium to cover the insurer’s operating expenses.
The profit arising from the difference between assumed and actual expense levels. An expense gain arises when actual expenses are lower than the loading in the product pricing.
Total operating expenses (excluding claims and reserve changes) as a percentage of net earned premium; measures the operational efficiency of the insurance business.
A premium rating technique adjusting renewal rates based on the scheme’s own claims history, blended with market expected rates using credibility weighting.
An examination command word requiring a clear, logical account of how or why something works or happens.

The ability of an insurer to provide a clear, non-technical explanation of why an AI model produced a specific output for a specific input; required by NDPA 2023 and NAICOM’s consumer protection framework.
A specific, informed, and unambiguous positive act of agreement to processing of special category data; stricter than standard consent; required for health data collected at underwriting.
Terms that are explicitly stated in the insurance policy document.

The structured information-gathering process through which a financial adviser collects all information needed to understand a client’s financial position, goals, and risk tolerance before making any recommendations.
Case-by-case reinsurance placement, negotiated individually for specific large or unusual risks; the cedant is not obligated to cede and the reinsurer is not obligated to accept.
Medical examination or report required for applicants above the non-medical limit or presenting specific risk factors.
A valid insurance claim incorrectly flagged by a fraud detection model as potentially fraudulent; the most damaging failure mode of a claims AI system.
The Shari’ah-compliant equivalent of life insurance, providing death and disability protection alongside savings through the PRA/PSA structure.
A formal legal opinion issued by an Islamic scholar or Shari’ah board on a matter of Islamic law.

t: FCIIN (Fellow of the Chartered Insurance Institute of Nigeria)
d: The Fellowship qualification; the highest CIIN designation, typically held by senior practitioners and leaders.
The issuer of FGN bonds and Sukuk, the primary fixed-income admissible assets for Nigerian insurers.
A health insurance payment model in which providers are paid a defined fee per service rendered.

t: Fellow of the Chartered Insurance Institute of Nigeria (FCIIN)
d: The highest CIIN qualification, representing distinguished achievement and typically required of or strongly preferred for CEO and senior leadership roles in licensed Nigerian insurers.

Federal Government of Nigeria bond: a fixed-income instrument issued by the DMO, denominated in Naira, with maturities from 2 to 30 years. The highest-quality domestic fixed-income instrument available to Nigerian life insurers.

t: FGN Bond (Federal Government of Nigeria Bond)
d: A sovereign debt security issued by the FGN through the Debt Management Office; the primary fixed-income admissible asset for Nigerian insurers.

Federal Government of Nigeria Sukuk bonds issued to fund renewable energy and climate adaptation infrastructure; an admissible, Shari’ah-compliant, ESG-aligned investment for Nigerian life and Takaful insurers.

A fraudulent insurance document issued by an unlicensed operator or without the backing of a genuine licensed insurer; a persistent problem in Nigeria’s compulsory motor insurance market, criminalised under NIIRA 2025.

The legal and professional obligation to act in another party’s best interest. Insurance brokers owe a strict fiduciary duty to their clients, including duties of care, disclosure, confidentiality, conflict avoidance, and following client instructions.
See Agency Force.
The provision of affordable, accessible, and appropriate financial services (including insurance, savings, credit, and payments) to populations currently excluded from the formal financial system.
The knowledge and skills required to make informed financial decisions. For insurance marketers, building financial literacy in the target population is a market development strategy.

An approach to quantifying the life insurance requirement by analysing the specific financial obligations the insured’s dependants would face on their death, including immediate expenses, debt clearance, income replacement, and education funding, less existing resources.
The PAS component generating data outputs for the financial accounting system, actuarial reporting, and NAICOM regulatory returns.
Assessment of the financial justification for the level of coverage requested, particularly for large sums assured, to prevent over-insurance.
Financial technology; technology companies providing financial services, typically in banking, payments, and lending.
Islamic commercial jurisprudence; the branch of Islamic law governing commercial transactions, including insurance.
The federal tax authority; governs the tax treatment of insurance premiums and benefits under PITA.
The proportion of customer queries resolved in the first interaction, without the customer needing to call back or escalate. A measure of both service quality and operational efficiency.
The initial notification by the claimant to the insurer of the occurrence of a potential claim.
Commission paid to an agent on the first-year premium of a new policy.
NAICOM’s standards for directors and key management personnel: qualifications, experience, integrity, and absence of disqualifying conduct.
NAICOM’s requirements for directors and key management personnel.
An agency structure with fewer management layers. Agents report directly to branch or regional management. Lower override cost but reduced supervision intensity.
A fixed additional annual premium per ₦1,000 sum assured applied to an impaired risk, regardless of the applicant’s age. Appropriate for impairments with approximately constant excess mortality.
Financial Markets Dealers Quotations; the securities exchange where FGN bonds, commercial paper, and other fixed-income instruments are listed and traded.
Nigeria’s primary fixed income and currency derivatives market, where FGN bonds, T-bills, and commercial paper are traded by institutional investors including life insurance companies.
A competitive strategy targeting a specific niche market with either lower cost or superior differentiation relative to broader competitors.
A reinsurance doctrine requiring the reinsurer to follow the cedant’s fortunes in claims settlement, provided the cedant acts in good faith and within the treaty terms.
The element of chance or uncertainty that must be present for a risk to be insurable; a loss that is certain to occur is not insurable.
Deliberate deception by the insured to obtain a benefit to which they are not entitled.
Observable characteristics of a claim that suggest potential fraud: inconsistent documentation, unusual timing, multiple policies on the same life, prior history.

A claim that involves deliberate misrepresentation, fabrication of evidence, or concealment of material facts, designed to obtain a benefit payment to which the claimant is not entitled under the true facts of the case.
Insurance coverage provided automatically without the need for individual medical underwriting; applies within the Free Cover Limit (FCL) in group life schemes.
The maximum sum assured per member covered in a group scheme without requiring individual medical evidence.
The sum assured per member provided without individual medical evidence in a group scheme.
The period after policy delivery during which the policyholder may cancel without penalty.
A defined period (typically 14–30 days) after policy delivery during which the policyholder may cancel the policy and receive a full premium refund.
Nigerian legislation giving citizens and organisations the right to request and receive public records and information held by government institutions including NAICOM and NBS.
The number of times a loss event occurs in a defined period within an insurance portfolio; one of the two components of the expected loss (frequency × severity).
An arrangement under which a licensed insurer issues a policy but cedes 100% of the risk to an unlicensed party; generally prohibited under NIIRA 2025.
A company holding its own insurance licence and operating the complete insurance value chain through digital infrastructure.
An organisational design in which each employee belongs to a single functional department and reports to that department’s head; dominant in Nigerian life insurance.
An annual percentage charge on the fund value of unit-linked policies, covering investment management costs and providing fee income to the insurer.
An investment professional responsible for making investment decisions for a defined portfolio.
The regulatory requirement that composite insurers maintain completely separate, identifiable funds for life and non-life insurance business, preventing cross-subsidisation between fund types.
A modest fixed sum payable quickly on death to cover immediate funeral expenses.
The directive implementing the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023 for data controllers and processors, effective September 2025.

Distinguished from insurance in that gambling creates a risk that would not otherwise exist (speculative risk), whereas insurance covers an existing risk (pure risk). Insurance is not gambling; the Maysir prohibition in Islamic finance draws this same distinction.
The Federal Government’s official publication for statutory instruments, regulations, and official notices; NAICOM uses the Gazette to issue legally binding circulars.
The default IFRS 17 measurement model, comprising three building blocks: Present Value of Future Cash Flows (PVFCF), Risk Adjustment (RA), and Contractual Service Margin (CSM).
The Shari’ah-compliant equivalent of general insurance, covering property, motor, and casualty risks for annual terms.

t: Geneva Papers on Risk and Insurance
d: A quarterly peer-reviewed journal published by the Geneva Association, covering insurance economics, financial stability, longevity, and the social role of insurance; the most prestigious applied insurance academic journal.
Excessive uncertainty or ambiguity in a contract; one of the three principal Shari’ah objections to conventional insurance.
The annual IAIS publication providing a comprehensive assessment of the global insurance sector’s financial condition, systemic risks, and supervisory developments.
Claims presented with all required documentation, enabling prompt assessment and settlement.
A defined period after the premium due date during which a premium may be paid without the policy lapsing.
The legal authority granted by a court to the executor of a will to administer the deceased’s estate; may be required before a death benefit can be paid where no valid nomination exists.
The total value of goods and services produced in Nigeria in a year; insurance penetration is typically expressed as a percentage of GDP.
The total premium paid by the policyholder, comprising the net premium (for pure risk coverage) plus expense and profit loadings.
A method of calculating the minimum solvency margin based on a percentage of gross written premium.
Total premiums billed by an insurer to policyholders in a period before any deduction for reinsurance ceded.
Life insurance covering a defined group (employees) under a single master policy, with each member’s beneficiaries receiving the sum assured on death.
The risk arising from the insurer’s membership of a group of companies, including contagion from group financial difficulties and governance risks.
The assessment of the collective mortality risk of a group of lives, using demographic and claims experience data rather than individual medical evidence.
A contractual commitment in a deferred annuity to convert the accumulated fund at a defined rate at the deferral date, regardless of future market conditions.
A standard medical underwriting requirement above defined sum assured thresholds in the Nigerian market, reflecting the impact of HIV/AIDS on life expectancy.
An NHIA-licensed organisation providing defined health services to enrollees for a fixed capitation premium.
Insurance paying a fixed daily cash benefit for each day of hospitalisation to compensate for indirect costs.

The present value of the future stream of income an individual is expected to generate over their remaining working life, net of personal consumption and income tax, representing the financial value of the individual to their dependants.
The global standard-setting body for insurance supervision, publishing the Insurance Core Principles (ICPs) and the GIMAR.

The global supervisory standards for insurance regulation published by the International Association of Insurance Supervisors. ICP 8 and ICP 16 set the ERM and ORSA expectations that NAICOM’s NIIRA 2025 requirements reflect.
The Nigerian actuarial professional body.
See Claims Incurred But Not Reported.
An examination command word requiring a list or specific naming of items without extended explanation.
The UK professional body for actuaries; many Nigerian actuaries qualify through the IFoA.
International Financial Reporting Standard 17 (Insurance Contracts), the accounting standard for insurance contracts effective for Nigerian listed insurers, replacing IFRS 4.

The International Financial Reporting Standard that replaced IFRS 4 for insurance contract accounting, effective January 2023. Requires insurance liabilities to be measured at current value using three measurement models: BBA/GMM, PAA, and VFA.

The IFRS standard governing the measurement of investment portfolios: classification and measurement of financial assets and liabilities; impairment; and hedge accounting. Affects how insurance investment portfolios are valued in IFRS financial statements.
Islamic Financial Services Board; the international prudential standard-setting body for Takaful and Islamic finance.
An Islamic leasing structure; used in Federal Government Sukuk issuances where assets are sold and leased back.
An examination command word requiring demonstration of a concept through examples or worked calculations.
A reduction in the carrying value of an investment asset to reflect a permanent or significant decline in its fair value.
Terms that are not explicitly stated in the policy but are implied by law or by the nature of the contract.
A complete list of all active policies with their key data; the definitive record of the insurer’s current policyholder obligations and the basis for actuarial reserving and NAICOM reporting.
The date on which insurance coverage commences under a policy.

The practice of designing products, processes, and interfaces to be accessible and usable by the widest possible range of customers, including those with disabilities, low literacy, or limited digital access.
The maximum sum assured expressed as a multiple of the applicant’s annual income. Declines with age to reflect the reducing number of remaining income-earning years.
Insurance replacing a proportion of the insured’s income during a period of disability caused by illness or injury.
The proportion of pre-retirement income needed to maintain the retiree’s standard of living; typically targeted at 70–80%.
A policy provision stating that after a defined period (typically 2 years), the insurer cannot contest the policy on grounds of misrepresentation, except in cases of fraud.
Restoration to the pre-loss financial position; the principle that insurance should not generate profit for the insured but should only compensate for actual loss.
Health insurance reimbursing actual costs at any provider, without network restriction.
An intermediary licensed to place business with multiple insurers, with a duty to recommend the most suitable product for the client from the available market.
A non-executive director with no material relationship to the company, its shareholders, or management.

A Board director who is independent of management and major shareholders, having no material business relationship with the company and no employment or family ties to executive directors or senior managers. INEDs provide objective challenge and oversight.

Insurance in which the benefit payment is triggered by an external index or parameter crossing a predefined threshold (e.g., rainfall below a drought threshold; river level above a flood threshold), rather than by assessment of the individual insured’s actual loss.
See Incontestability Clause.
Life insurance on a single insured life, governed by a policy issued to a named policyholder.
The assessment of the mortality risk of a specific individual through disclosure, medical evidence, and financial analysis.
Partnering with individuals who have built trusted social media audiences to create and distribute content about the insurer’s brand or products to those audiences.
A formal legal inquiry conducted by a coroner into the circumstances and cause of a sudden, unexplained, violent, or suspicious death. Inquest findings may affect the insurer’s claims assessment.

The legal requirement that the policyholder must stand to suffer a financial loss from the occurrence of the insured event. In life insurance, a person has an unlimited insurable interest in their own life and a defined insurable interest in the lives of specified others (spouses, debtors).
A mechanism for transferring risk from an individual or organisation to an insurer, in exchange for a premium, whereby the insurer pools many small premiums to pay the larger losses of the few.
See Agent.
A company registered with NAICOM and a member of NCRIB that places insurance business with insurers on behalf of clients. The broker is the legal agent of the client, not the insurer.
The legal agreement between the insurer and the policyholder setting out rights and obligations.

The IAIS’s globally adopted benchmark standards for insurance supervision, covering corporate governance, risk management, solvency, valuation, conduct of business, and supervisory cooperation; the framework to which NAICOM’s regulatory development including NIIRA 2025 is explicitly aligned.

The period during which an individual’s financial obligations exceed their accumulated assets, making life insurance the only affordable way to provide financial security to dependants in the event of premature death.
The annual regulatory levy paid by licensed insurers to NAICOM, calculated as a percentage of gross premium income.
A proposed alternative dispute resolution mechanism for policyholder complaints under NIIRA 2025, providing a faster and less costly route than formal litigation.

Total insurance premium income as a percentage of GDP; the primary measure of an insurance market’s depth. Nigeria’s insurance penetration is currently below 0.5% of GDP, compared to 3–5% in comparable emerging markets.
The risk of loss arising from the insurer’s underwriting activities: adverse mortality, morbidity, longevity, lapse, or expense experience.
The application of technology to improve the efficiency, accessibility, and personalisation of insurance products and services.
NAICOM’s regulatory framework for technology-driven insurance innovations, including the Partnering Insurtech and Standalone Insurtech licensing tracks and the regulatory sandbox.
The profit source arising from the difference between the assumed and actual investment return on the policy reserve.
The risk of loss arising from adverse movements in interest rates, particularly for long-duration liabilities such as annuities and endowments.
A proportionate bonus paid on a death claim occurring between annual bonus declaration dates, representing the partial-year bonus earned up to the date of death.
Any person or company that facilitates the sale of insurance between an insurer and a policyholder; includes agents and brokers.
The independent assurance function providing the Board with objective assessment of controls and risk management; the third line of defence.
A legal action by the insurer where competing beneficiaries make conflicting claims to the same benefit, asking the court to determine the rightful claimant.
The legal situation arising when a person dies without a valid will; the distribution of their estate is governed by applicable inheritance law.
The Board committee responsible for overseeing the Investment Policy Statement and investment portfolio performance.

The set of objectives, constraints, and guidelines that govern how a life insurer’s investment portfolio is managed, including return targets, risk tolerance, ALM requirements, admissible asset classes, and regulatory compliance obligations.
The Board-approved document defining the insurer’s investment objectives, risk tolerance, asset allocation strategy, and prohibited instruments.
Total investment income as a percentage of average invested assets; the primary measure of the portfolio’s income-generating efficiency.
A policy whose benefits are linked to the market value of underlying investment funds chosen by the policyholder, also called a unit-linked policy.
Reinsurance accepted by a company from other insurers or reinsurers; the company acts as a reinsurer.
The network of physical devices embedded with sensors that collect and transmit data; used in parametric trigger monitoring and telematics.

The international standard for risk management principles, framework, and process, published by the International Organization for Standardization. Provides the universal language and process architecture for ERM across all sectors.
An automated telephone system routing incoming calls through a menu of options; improved IVR design reduces call abandonment and increases first-call resolution.
Nigeria’s first fully fledged Islamic bank; a potential Takaful distribution partner.
A life annuity that continues to pay a reduced income to the surviving spouse after the annuitant’s death.
A policy on two or more lives, typically paying the sum assured on the first death.
The leading academic journal in insurance economics and actuarial science, published by the American Risk and Insurance Association.
Life or disability insurance on a business key person, with the business as policyholder and beneficiary, protecting against the financial loss from the key person’s death or incapacity.
A quantitative metric that provides advance warning that a risk is increasing toward or beyond the tolerance threshold. Effective KRIs are measurable, timely, predictive, actionable, and owned.

Life or disability insurance taken out by a business on the life of a key individual whose death or disability would materially harm the business, providing the capital to replace the individual, service debt, or fund business continuity.

The process of identifying, verifying, and understanding the insurance customer and the source of the funds used to pay premiums, as required by the Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act 2022 and NAICOM AML/CFT guidelines.
A specific, measurable metric for evaluating performance against targets.
The process of verifying the identity and risk profile of policyholders and other business relationships, required under the MLPPA 2022 and NAICOM AML guidelines.
The termination of an insurance policy due to non-payment of premium after the expiry of any applicable grace period.
The systematic process of identifying at-risk policies (those with missed premiums), diagnosing the cause, and intervening before the policy moves from active to lapsed status.
An AI/ML model identifying at-risk policyholders based on behavioural signals to enable targeted conservation.
The profit source arising from the difference between assumed and actual lapse rates.
An ML model that assigns each in-force policy a probability of lapsing within a defined future period, enabling targeted conservation intervention.
The proportion of in-force policies that terminate (lapse) in a defined period, typically measured at 13 months.

The statistical principle that as the number of independent risk units in an insurance pool increases, the actual loss experience converges toward the expected (average) loss, enabling accurate pricing.
One of the six legal grounds permitting personal data processing under NDPA 2023: consent, contract performance, legal obligation, vital interests, public task, or legitimate interests.
A prospective customer who has expressed interest in or been identified as a potential buyer of an insurance product.
A metric that assesses the likelihood of a marketing-generated lead converting to a policy, based on qualification criteria such as income, intent level, and product fit.
The process of ranking prospects by likelihood of converting to a policyholder, based on demographic, behavioural, and engagement signals, enabling prioritisation of the highest-value opportunities.
Legal authority granted by a court to administer the estate of a person who died intestate.
Legal authority granted by a court to an administrator to handle the estate of a person who died intestate (without a will).
A life annuity paying the same nominal income throughout the annuitant’s life.
Term assurance with a fixed sum assured throughout the policy term.
An IFRS 17 requirement to confirm that the insurer’s insurance contract liabilities are sufficient to cover future cash outflows.
The NAICOM authorisation permitting a company to transact a defined class of insurance business in Nigeria.
The expected number of additional years of life remaining for a person of a given age, calculated from a mortality table.
A statistical table showing the probability of survival or death at each age, used as the foundation of life insurance underwriting and pricing.

A statistical table tracking a cohort of lives from a defined starting age, recording the number surviving to each subsequent age and the derived probability of death (qx) and survival (px) at each age.
The maximum amount a reinsurer will accept on a single risk under a treaty.
The risk that the insurer cannot convert assets to cash quickly enough to meet its claims and operational obligations.
A broker approved by Lloyd’s to submit risks to underwriters in the Lloyd’s market. Few Nigerian brokers hold direct accreditation; most access Lloyd’s through London correspondent brokers.
The international insurance and reinsurance marketplace in London through which specialist syndicates underwrite complex, unusual, and large risks. Access is restricted to Lloyd’s accredited brokers.
An amount added to the net premium to cover the insurer’s expenses, profit margin, and contingency reserve.
An additional premium charged above the standard rate to compensate the insurer for a higher-than-average risk.
The risk that annuitants live longer than the mortality assumption, requiring more years of annuity payments than priced for.
The risk that annuitants outlive the mortality assumption, requiring more years of income payments than priced for.
Claims incurred as a percentage of premiums earned; the primary measure of underwriting experience.
The right of an RSA holder to withdraw up to 25% of their RSA balance before converting the remainder to an annuity or PW.
A life table function: the number of lives from the original cohort (radix) that are still alive at exact age x.
A subset of AI in which systems learn from data to improve performance without being explicitly programmed.

The annual review of a life insurer’s financial condition required by NIIRA 2025, conducted by the Statutory Actuary, producing a prudent-basis assessment of reserve adequacy and the actuarial certificate.
Insurance required by law, including the mandatory group life obligation under the PRA 2014, mandatory credit life under NIIRA 2025, and TPMI for motor vehicles.
The valuation of investment assets at their current market price, rather than historical cost.
The behaviour of insurers and their agents toward policyholders and prospective customers; regulated by NIIRA 2025’s consumer protection framework.

NAICOM’s supervisory review of a licensed insurer’s treatment of policyholders: claims settlement compliance, product suitability, agent conduct, complaint handling, and compulsory insurance compliance.
Specific competitive and commercial information about the market environment, typically gathered from competitor monitoring, industry events, distribution channel feedback, and regulatory sources.
The policy documentation format used in the Lloyd’s and London company markets, recording the agreed terms and the subscribed lines of each participating underwriter.
The risk of loss from adverse movements in market prices (interest rates, equity prices, property values, exchange rates).
The quantitative estimation of the total potential premium income or policy volume available in a defined market segment.

The commercial contract governing a bancassurance partnership between a bank and an insurer, covering exclusivity, product shelf, commission structure, premium remittance, compliance obligations, and data sharing.
Any fact that would influence a prudent insurer’s decision to accept the risk or the terms on which it would do so.
An organisational design in which employees have dual reporting lines, functional and project or business unit, enabling cross-functional collaboration at the cost of greater structural complexity.
The sum payable to the policyholder at the end of the policy term under an endowment or savings-linked policy, provided the insured survives to the maturity date.

A claim made by a policyholder on the expiry of the defined policy term of an endowment or savings policy, where the life assured is still alive. The insurer is obligated to pay the maturity sum assured and any accumulated bonuses.
Gambling or speculative gain; one of the three Shari’ah objections to conventional insurance.
A Foundation and Diploma examination question format presenting four options, one of which is correct.
The most senior executive of the company, accountable to the Board for overall management.
The rate of increase in healthcare costs, typically exceeding general CPI; a critical risk in health insurance pricing.
The physician retained by the insurer to advise on medical underwriting decisions and to interpret clinical evidence.
Documentation required to substantiate a disability or critical illness claim: hospital records, specialist reports, pathology results.
A clinical examination of an applicant by a NAICOM-approved medical examiner, required above defined sum assured thresholds or for complex risks.

Insurance designed for the low-income population, offered at a premium that is affordable relative to the target population’s income, and distributed through channels appropriate for their circumstances (mobile money, cooperatives, MFBs, USSD).
A CBN-licensed financial institution serving the lower-income and small business segments. MFBs are permitted corporate agents for microinsurance products under NAICOM guidelines.
Simple, low-premium, high-volume insurance products designed for low-income populations, typically distributed through community, mobile, or cooperative channels.
The minimum paid-up capital prescribed by NIIRA 2025 for licensed insurers; the threshold for initial and ongoing licensing.

The sale of an insurance product to a customer through dishonest, misleading, or unsuitable conduct, including misrepresentation of product terms, omission of material exclusions, unsuitable product recommendation, or use of pressure tactics.
A false statement of material fact made by the proposer at application, which may entitle the insurer to avoid the policy.
