The Money Laundering (Prevention and Prohibition) Act 2022; the primary Nigerian AML/CFT legislation applicable to insurers.
The examiner’s indicative ideal answer, typically providing more information than the maximum mark-earning response.
The degradation of an AI model’s predictive accuracy over time as the real-world patterns it was trained on change; requires ongoing monitoring and periodic retraining.
The framework of policies, processes, and accountability structures ensuring that AI models are documented, validated, monitored, tested for fairness, and deployed with appropriate human oversight.
The risk that an AI or ML model produces incorrect outputs due to flawed development, poor data quality, or changed conditions.
A variant of co-insurance in which the reinsurer assumes its share of risk but the cedant retains the physical reserve assets, paying the reinsurer an interest credit on the retained reserve amount.
A defined unit of study within a CIIN qualification, assessed by a single examination paper.

A specific customer interaction at which the customer forms a definitive impression of the organisation that either builds or destroys their trust. The claim payment is the ultimate moment of truth in insurance.

The designated senior officer responsible for receiving internal suspicious transaction reports, assessing them, and filing Suspicious Transaction Reports (STRs) with the Nigerian Financial Intelligence Unit (NFIU).
A brand structure in which all products are marketed under a single corporate brand identity. All marketing investment reinforces the same brand.
The tendency for the presence of insurance to reduce the insured’s incentive to prevent loss or moderate claims behaviour. Managed through co-payments, deductibles, and claims investigation.
The risk that an applicant has concealed information, misrepresented their circumstances, or has an incentive to claim that influenced their application.

A simplified underwriting approach under which individual medical evidence is waived, but claims arising from pre-existing conditions within a defined exclusion period are not covered. Widely used in microinsurance for practicability.
The incidence of illness or disability within a population; used in health insurance underwriting and pricing.
The statistical frequency of death within a population; the foundational risk concept in life assurance pricing.
Projections of the expected annual rate of improvement in mortality rates, incorporated into annuity pricing and reserving.
The analysis of actual deaths within the insurer’s portfolio against the expected mortality from the pricing table; essential input for profit source analysis.
The profit source arising from the difference between assumed and actual mortality experience.
The probability that a person aged exactly x will die before reaching age x+1, as expressed in a life table.
A life policy designed to repay the outstanding mortgage balance on death or disability of the borrower.
An Islamic profit-sharing contract in which one party provides capital and the other provides management skill; used in the Mudarabah Takaful model.
National Agency for Food and Drug Administration and Control; relevant to health insurance in certifying drugs covered under HMO formularies.
The National Insurance Commission; the apex regulator of the insurance industry in Nigeria, established under the NAICOM Act 1997 and with enhanced powers under NIIRA 2025.
The legislation establishing NAICOM as Nigeria’s insurance regulator, now read together with NIIRA 2025.

Regulatory guidelines effective 1 August 2025, establishing licensing frameworks for Standalone Insurtech (₦1–1.5bn capital) and Partnering Insurtech (₦10m) entities operating digital insurance distribution in Nigeria.
A controlled regulatory environment in which Insurtech entrants can test innovative insurance models under NAICOM supervision before committing to full licensing, established under NIIRA 2025.
The NIIRA 2025-mandated pool providing compensation to victims of uninsured or underinsured compulsory insurance claims, funded by licensed insurer contributions and administered by NAICOM.
The federal regulator of Nigeria’s pension system, licensing PFAs and PFCs and supervising the RLA market.
AI technology enabling computers to understand and generate human language; applied in insurance for processing medical records, chatbots, and document review.
The government statistical agency; a key source of household income, expenditure, and demographic data for insurance market research.
Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023; the primary data protection law applicable to insurers as data controllers.
The primary data protection legislation applicable to Nigerian insurers as data controllers, imposing obligations on consent, data minimisation, breach notification, and data subject rights.

The NDPA 2023 provision (Section 35) giving data subjects the right not to be subject to decisions based solely on automated processing that produce legal or significant effects; requires human review of AI-driven adverse decisions in insurance.
The regulatory risk arising from inadequate data protection practices (insufficient consent, breach notification failure, unauthorised data sharing) under the Nigeria Data Protection Act 2023.
The initial stage of the broking process in which the broker assesses the client’s risk profile to identify all insurable exposures and determine the appropriate insurance programme.

The difference between the sum assured and the policy reserve at any given duration. Represents the amount the insurer must pay from current funds (not from the accumulated reserve) if the insured dies in that year.
Net written premium adjusted for the change in unearned premium reserve.
The premium required purely to fund expected claims, before any expense or profit loading; the actuarially calculated pure risk premium.
A customer loyalty metric calculated as the percentage of Promoters (those scoring 9–10 on a recommendation likelihood question) minus the percentage of Detractors (those scoring 0–6).
The amount of risk the cedant retains on its own account after cession to reinsurers.
Gross written premium minus reinsurance premium ceded.
New Business Value divided by Present Value of New Business Premium; the primary metric of new business profitability.

The PAS module that handles the journey from application intake through underwriting to policy issuance, capturing all proposal form data and routing the application through the underwriting workflow.

The first-year cash flow deficit arising when the initial expenses of a new life insurance policy (commission, underwriting, issue costs) exceed the first-year premium. Co-insurance reinsurance partially addresses new business strain through the ceding commission.
The present value of future shareholder profits from policies written in the current period.
The Nigerian Stock Exchange and its affiliated markets; the primary equity market for Shari’ah-screened investments and listed insurer securities.
The federal body responsible for licensing and supervising HMOs and working toward universal health coverage under the NHIA Act 2022.
The trade association for licensed Nigerian insurers; a collective voice for the industry with NAICOM and the public.

The primary Nigerian data protection legislation, assented to on 12 June 2023, establishing comprehensive data subject rights, data processing obligations, and the Nigeria Data Protection Commission (NDPC) as the enforcement authority.

t: Nigerian Council of Registered Insurance Brokers (NCRIB)
d: The statutory professional body for insurance brokers in Nigeria, responsible for maintaining the broker register, setting professional standards, and co-regulating the broking profession alongside NAICOM.
A federal government-linked reinsurance company providing domestic reinsurance capacity; part of the domestic cession obligation market.
An application returned to the distributor or agent because it is incomplete, inconsistent, or missing required documentation or signatures.
See entry in Section 8.

The Act No. 2 of 2025 that consolidates and replaces the Insurance Act 2003, introducing RBC, Insurtech licensing, enhanced consumer protection, and updated capital requirements. The foundational regulatory instrument for this work.
The federal agency managing the national identity system; NIN verification is a key KYC tool for Nigerian insurers.
The unique identifier issued by NIMC; required for insurance KYC and policy issuance.
A NAICOM-issued approval authorising a specific transaction or arrangement (e.g., a change of ownership, a reinsurance arrangement) that requires prior NAICOM approval.
The fundamental principle that insurance coverage does not commence until the first premium is received; codified in NIIRA 2025.
The formal designation of who will receive the policy benefit on death.
The failure to reveal a material fact to the insurer at the time of application.
A Board member without an executive management role; provides independent oversight.
Insurance other than life assurance; includes property, casualty, marine, motor, and aviation insurance; regulated by NAICOM under a separate licence class.
The maximum sum assured for which an application may be accepted on the basis of the proposal form alone, without requiring additional medical evidence.
The maximum sum assured up to which a life insurer will issue a policy based solely on the applicant’s health declarations, without requiring a medical examination.
A life policy that does not participate in the insurer’s surplus; benefits are fixed at policy inception.

A reinsurance arrangement in which the reinsurer’s obligation is triggered only when claims exceed a defined threshold (priority or attachment point). The reinsurer does not receive a proportionate share of premium. Includes excess of loss and stop loss.
An application or proposal form that is returned to the agent or sales team by the underwriting function because it is incomplete, contains errors, or lacks required supporting documentation.
A customer loyalty metric based on the proportion of customers who would recommend the insurer’s products and services to others.
A government-linked domestic reinsurer.
A sequenced series of marketing communications (typically email or WhatsApp) that guide a prospect from initial awareness through education to a purchase decision over a defined period.
A categorisation of occupations by hazard level used to determine the appropriate premium loading for occupational mortality risk.
A classification (typically Class 1 to 4) assigned to an occupation based on its physical risk relative to the standard office/professional risk assumed in the standard mortality table.
An additional premium loading applied where the applicant’s occupation is associated with higher-than-average mortality risk.
A policy that covers events that occur during the policy period, regardless of when the claim is made. Distinguished from a claims-made policy.
Technology converting printed or handwritten documents into machine-readable text; used in insurance for processing medical examination reports, hospital records, and identity documents.
The basic contract formation mechanism; in insurance, the proposal form is typically the offer and the insurer’s acceptance letter or cover note is the acceptance.
A goal-setting framework using ambitious qualitative objectives and specific measurable results; a quarterly execution complement to the Balanced Scorecard.

A United Kingdom mortality table based on assured lives experience around 1992. Used in Nigerian practice as a reference benchmark and for expatriate/group products, with appropriate adjustment factors for the Nigerian mortality environment.
A customer experience design in which the customer can move seamlessly between channels (branch, digital, agent, WhatsApp, USSD) without losing progress or repeating information.
The sharing of financial data between institutions through open APIs, enabling new product innovations and embedded insurance.
The risk of loss from inadequate or failed internal processes, people, or systems, or from external events.
The main insuring clause of the policy, defining the insurer’s primary obligation.
A trusted external data source delivering real-world data (weather, commodity prices) to a blockchain smart contract for parametric trigger verification.
The shared values, beliefs, behaviours, and unwritten rules that characterise how work gets done in an organisation, shaped primarily by the behaviours modelled and rewarded by senior leaders.
The insurer’s annual self-assessment of its risk profile, risk appetite, and capital adequacy, required under NIIRA 2025.

A scenario included in the Own Risk and Solvency Assessment evaluating the insurer’s financial resilience under a defined climate change pathway (e.g., 2°C warming by 2050), assessing impacts on mortality assumptions, health claims, lapse rates, and investment portfolio.
An examination command word requiring a structured summary without full detail; less depth than ‘describe’.
Medical treatment that does not require overnight hospital admission.
Reinsurance ceded by an insurer to reinsurers to reduce its net exposure.
An additional commission paid to a supervising agent or agency manager, calculated as a percentage of the new business production generated by the agents they supervise.
Commission paid by the insurer to an agency manager or unit manager on the production of the agents in their unit.

A comprehensive forward-looking internal assessment of the insurer’s material risks and its current and projected solvency position under base and stress scenarios. Mandatory under NIIRA 2025; submitted annually to NAICOM.
The amount of share capital actually received from shareholders; used as the basis for the minimum capital requirement under NIIRA 2025.
A policy on which the policyholder has ceased paying premiums and which continues in force with a reduced sum assured.

The reduced sum assured for which a policy is kept in force when the policyholder ceases premium payments before maturity. No further premiums are required; the policy continues until maturity at the lower benefit level.
The risk that a widespread disease event significantly increases mortality claims across the insurer’s life portfolio simultaneously.

The practice of operating both the old and new PAS simultaneously for a defined period after go-live, comparing daily outputs to identify and resolve discrepancies before decommissioning the old system.
Insurance that pays a defined benefit automatically when a measurable index (rainfall, wind speed) reaches a trigger level, without requiring individual loss assessment.
The specific index value or event (rainfall below threshold, river level above threshold) that must be observed for a parametric insurance benefit payment to be automatically executed.
On equal footing; relevant in the context of co-insurance where all participating insurers share claims in proportion to their participation.
The collective Takaful mutual fund into which Tabaru’ contributions are pooled and from which claims are paid.
The individual savings account within a Family Takaful plan, belonging to the participant and invested in Shari’ah-compliant instruments.
A life insurance policy under which the policyholder is entitled to share in the distributable surplus of the with-profit fund, received as reversionary, terminal, or interim bonuses.
A life policy that participates in the insurer’s distributable surplus through the declaration of reversionary and terminal bonuses.
The core software system managing an insurer’s policy records, premium transactions, claims, and customer data.
National Pension Commission; see Section 15.
A PenCom-licensed company managing individual RSA contributions and investments.
A PenCom-licensed institution physically holding and safeguarding RSA assets.
The primary legislation governing the Nigerian CPS, mandatory group life, RLA framework, and PFA licensing.

A multiplicative increase in the standard premium applied to an impaired risk (e.g., 150% of standard premium). Appropriate for impairments with excess mortality proportionate to baseline age-specific mortality.

A formal, time-bound plan agreed between an employee with performance deficiencies and their line manager, specifying the improvement targets and support required, with defined consequences if targets are not met.

Paid digital advertising designed to generate measurable direct responses (leads, applications, sign-ups) with trackable cost-per-acquisition metrics. Includes paid social media ads and search engine ads.
The specific cause of loss against which insurance is provided (e.g., death, disability, critical illness).
A rider paying a lump sum if the insured employee becomes permanently unable to work.
The proportion of policies in force that remain active at a defined anniversary (typically 13 months); the inverse of lapse rate.

A bonus paid when the proportion of an agent’s in-force book that remains active exceeds a defined persistency rate. Aligns the agent’s financial interest with the insurer’s interest in policy retention.
The proportion of policies issued in a defined cohort that remain in force at a subsequent duration (13 months or 25 months). A key quality indicator for all distribution channels.
A security incident leading to accidental or unlawful destruction, loss, alteration, unauthorised disclosure of, or access to personal data.

The structured process of helping an individual or family identify financial goals, understand the risks that could prevent them from reaching those goals, and design and implement a strategy using savings, insurance, investment, debt management, and tax planning to address each goal and risk.
A long-term savings and life insurance product for self-employed individuals outside the mandatory CPS.

A structured environmental scanning framework analysing Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Environmental, and Legal forces in the macro-environment that create opportunities and threats for the organisation.
A structured commercial arrangement between a life insurer and one or more PFAs, under which the PFA refers RSA holders approaching retirement to the insurer for annuity quotation and conversion.

A hybrid service delivery model combining physical presence (agent, branch) with digital enablement (app, USSD, WhatsApp), providing human interaction where needed and digital efficiency for routine transactions.
The risk of financial loss arising from the physical impacts of climate change, including acute events (floods, storms) and chronic shifts (rising temperatures, changing precipitation).
The primary Nigerian income tax legislation; governs the tax treatment of insurance premiums and retirement savings.
A document prepared by the broker describing a client’s risk in detail for presentation to insurers during the market placement process. Also called a market submission or submission document.
The written insurance contract between the insurer and the policyholder, setting out the parties’ rights and obligations.

The core software system that creates, stores, and manages all insurance policy records across the policy lifecycle, from application through to termination. The system of record for all policyholder obligations.
The insurer’s right to treat a policy as void from inception (ab initio) where material non-disclosure or misrepresentation by the proposer is established. The effect is that no claim is payable.
Fixed charges levied on policyholders to recover administrative costs, providing recurring non-underwriting income independent of premium level.
A loan made by the insurer to the policyholder against the surrender value of an in-force life policy.
The PAS module handling all changes to an in-force policy after issuance, including endorsements, reinstatements, policy loans, and beneficiary changes, with complete audit trail.
Funds held by the insurer to meet its future obligations under in-force life policies.

The amount the insurer must hold in its balance sheet at any duration to meet all future policy obligations. Calculated by the prospective method (EPV of future benefits less EPV of future premiums) or the retrospective method.

The reinstatement of a lapsed policy, typically involving repayment of overdue premiums and satisfying any re-underwriting requirements. Revival campaigns target lapsed policyholders with incentives to reinstate.
The person or entity who enters into the insurance contract with the insurer and is responsible for paying the premium.
A person who holds or has held a prominent public function, including government ministers, senior civil servants, and senior military officers. PEP transactions require enhanced due diligence.
A collective arrangement under which multiple insurers share a specific category of risk; used for risks that are too large or specialised for individual insurers to cover alone.

A framework for analysing competitive dynamics in an industry through five structural forces: threat of new entrants, bargaining power of buyers, bargaining power of suppliers, threat of substitutes, and intensity of competitive rivalry.
Total investment income generated by the investment portfolio as a proportion of average invested assets during the period.
See Investment Yield.
A medical examination report on the cause of death; may be required in accidental death benefit claims where the cause of death is disputed.
The insurer’s advance approval for a defined healthcare service, required before the service is provided.
A health condition that existed before the insurance coverage commenced; typically subject to a waiting period or exclusion.
The consideration paid by the policyholder to the insurer in exchange for coverage.
The simplified IFRS 17 measurement model applicable to short-duration contracts (annual renewable term, group life), analogous to the unearned premium reserve approach used for general insurance.

The automatic deduction of insurance premiums from a mobile money wallet on a scheduled basis, authorised by the customer at enrolment. The most effective premium collection mechanism for mobile microinsurance.
The policy clause specifying the premium amount, frequency, and payment terms.
The PAS module managing premium billing generation, premium receipt recording, grace period tracking, lapse processing, and premium reconciliation.
Total premiums received from policyholders in a defined period.
The daily process of matching expected premium income (from the PAS billing schedule) against actual bank receipts, with investigation of unmatched items.
A tax on insurance premiums levied in some jurisdictions; the specific Nigerian treatment is governed by FIRS guidance.
A segregated bank account maintained by a broker specifically for client insurance premiums, held in trust for the insurer until remittance and for the client in the event of return premiums.
The current worth of future cash flows, discounted at an appropriate interest rate.

A legal status declared by a court in respect of a missing person who has been continuously absent and unheard of for the statutory period (typically seven years under the Nigerian Evidence Act). A declaration of presumed death enables a life assurance claim to proceed.
The principle that data protection is built into information systems and processes from the outset, not added as an afterthought; required by NDPA 2023 and GAID 2025 for DCPMIs.
The legal process of proving the validity of a will and authorising the executor to administer the estate.
NAICOM’s review and approval of an insurer’s proposed new product before it can be marketed; governed by the NAICOM product approval guidelines.

The structured, gate-based process through which a life insurer transforms consumer insight and market opportunity into a commercially viable, actuarially sound, and regulatorily compliant new product.
The curated range of insurance products approved for distribution through a specific bancassurance channel, designed for simplicity and alignment with the bank’s customer interaction moments.

The sequential relationship between agent activity (prospecting contacts), pipeline (appointments, proposals), and production (cases submitted and issued). Each stage’s conversion rate determines the next stage’s volume.
Insurance protecting professionals against claims of negligent advice or service; relevant to financial advisers and insurance practitioners.

Insurance covering the broker against claims by clients for financial loss arising from the broker’s professional negligence, errors, or omissions. Mandatory for all licensed Nigerian insurance brokers.
The decomposition of life insurance profit into mortality (C1), interest (C2), expense (C3), and lapse (C4) components.

The decomposition of life insurance profit into four components: mortality profit (C1), interest profit (C2), expense profit (C3), and lapse profit (C4), each representing the difference between the pricing assumption and actual experience.
The CPS alternative to the RLA, in which the RSA balance remains invested by the PFA and the holder draws a defined monthly income.

The documentary evidence submitted to the insurer to establish that the life assured has died. In Nigeria, the primary document is the National Population Commission death certificate, supported by a medical certificate of cause of death.
Documentation provided by the claimant substantiating the occurrence and extent of the claimed loss.

A reinsurance arrangement in which the cedant and the reinsurer share both the premium and the risk in defined proportions. Premium and claims are allocated in the same ratio. Includes quota share and surplus treaties.
A reinsurance structure (quota share or surplus) in which premiums and losses are shared in defined proportions.
The application document completed by the proposer seeking insurance, through which material facts are disclosed to the insurer.
The person who applies for insurance; typically becomes the policyholder if the application is accepted.
The policy reserve calculated as the expected present value of future benefits minus the expected present value of future premiums, using the valuation basis.
The hospitals, clinics, and pharmacies contracted by the HMO to provide services to enrollees.
The net premium required solely to fund expected claims, without any expense or profit loading.
A risk that can only result in loss or no change; it cannot produce a gain. Pure risks are insurable; speculative risks (which can produce either gain or loss) are not.
The probability that a life alive at exact age x will survive to age x+1. px = 1 − qx.

An agency structure with multiple management layers, each earning override commission on the production of the layer below. Provides intensive supervision and coaching but carries higher override cost.
An interest-free loan; in Takaful, the operator may provide a Qard Hassan to cover a PRA deficit, to be repaid from future surpluses.
A proportional reinsurance treaty under which the cedant cedes a fixed percentage of all premiums and losses across a defined class of business.

A proportional reinsurance treaty under which a fixed percentage of every risk within the treaty scope is ceded to the reinsurer. The same percentage applies to premiums and claims on every ceded policy.
The probability that a life alive at exact age x will die before reaching age x+1. qx = dx / lx. The fundamental building block of all life insurance premium calculations.
The application of an additional premium loading to a substandard risk.
The Takaful equivalent of reinsurance, structured on Shari’ah-compliant mutual contribution principles.
Direct or indirect investment in property as part of the insurer’s investment portfolio; an admissible asset class under NAICOM guidelines.
The process of increasing an insurer’s paid-up capital to meet NIIRA 2025’s new minimum capital requirements.
An examination command word requiring the candidate to make and justify a specific course of action based on the facts of the question.
A mandatory document cataloguing every personal data processing activity: purposes, legal bases, data categories, data subjects, retention periods, security measures, and third parties.
A recommendation by an existing customer or professional contact directing a prospective customer to the insurer or agent.
A structured incentive that rewards existing policyholders for introducing new customers, leveraging social proof and personal endorsement as acquisition tools.
The risk of loss or constraint arising from changes in the regulatory framework, NAICOM enforcement action, or regulatory non-compliance.
The NAICOM framework allowing Insurtech companies to test innovative insurance models under controlled supervision before full licensing.

A controlled regulatory environment established by NAICOM’s Insurtech Guidelines in which Insurtech companies can test innovative insurance models under close NAICOM supervision before committing to full licensing.

A controlled regulatory environment in which Insurtech entrants may test innovative insurance models, including microinsurance delivery innovations, under NAICOM supervision before committing to full licensing.
The restoration of a lapsed policy to full force, usually on payment of all outstanding premiums and satisfaction of the insurer’s reinstatement underwriting requirements.

A contract under which a direct insurer (the cedant) transfers a defined portion of the insurance risks it has accepted from policyholders to one or more reinsurers, in exchange for a proportionate share of the premium.
An intermediary who arranges reinsurance placements on behalf of cedants; regulated under NIIRA 2025.
The application of the broking function to the placement of reinsurance on behalf of direct insurers (cedants) with reinsurers.
The PAS module calculating and recording reinsurance cessions under treaty arrangements, generating treaty statements, and tracking reinsurance recoveries on claims.
The commission paid by the reinsurer to the cedant under a proportional treaty, compensating the cedant for its acquisition and administration expenses.
The amount recovered by the cedant from reinsurers in respect of a ceded claim.
The maximum sum assured that the cedant retains on its own account for any single life risk, above which the excess is ceded to reinsurers.
The master reinsurance agreement between the cedant and reinsurer, setting out the terms under which risks are ceded and recovered.
The risk that, when a bond matures, the reinvested proceeds earn a lower rate than the original bond.
The Board committee setting remuneration policy for the Board and senior management.
Term assurance that may be renewed for a further period without evidence of health, at the prevailing premium rates for the attained age.
The continuation of an insurance policy for a further period, typically annually, on payment of the renewal premium.
Commission paid to an agent on the renewal premium of an in-force policy in subsequent years.
A statement made by the proposer to the insurer at the time of application; if materially false, it may entitle the insurer to avoid the policy.
The insurer’s formal refusal to pay a claim, typically on grounds of non-disclosure, policy exclusion, or policy lapse.
The cancellation of a contract, returning both parties to their original positions.
A structured schedule assigning specific monitoring and analysis activities to defined months throughout the year, ensuring systematic coverage of all key data sources.
The organisational unit responsible for generating the market intelligence, consumer insights, and operational analytics that inform strategic and product decisions in a life insurance company.
A monthly meeting between the research/CI function and strategy, product, and distribution leadership at which research findings are translated into management implications and actions.
Funds held by an insurer to meet future policy obligations (claims reserves, life policy reserves, IBNR provisions).
The remaining level of risk after controls and mitigation measures have been applied.

The distribution channel in which individual agents build personal relationships with prospective policyholders to sell individual life insurance products, typically organised in a pyramid hierarchy of agents, unit managers, branch managers, and regional directors.
The direct client-facing broking model in which the broker has a relationship with the ultimate insurance buyer and places insurance directly with insurers.
The net amount of risk the cedant keeps on its own account; defined in the treaty as a retention limit (per life or per event) or a retention percentage.
The maximum net amount at risk that the direct insurer retains on any single life for its own account, net of reinsurance. Amounts above the retention are ceded to the reinsurer.
The immediate life annuity product available under the CPS, providing guaranteed retirement income in exchange for RSA funds.
The individual pension savings account held by each CPS contributor, managed by a PFA.

A senior, highly qualified member of the annuity sales team who advises retirees on annuity options, conducts retirement income planning, and manages the fund transfer process from the PFA to the insurer.
The policy reserve calculated as the accumulated value of past premium income minus the accumulated value of past claims and expenses, using the valuation basis.
The revenue generated per naira spent on paid digital advertising. ROAS = Revenue from Ads ÷ Cost of Ads.
The complete map of an insurer’s income sources, their relative sizes, their interdependencies, and the management disciplines required to sustain and grow each.
A stress test that identifies the scenario under which the insurer’s solvency ratio would breach the regulatory minimum. Required as part of the ORSA under NIIRA 2025.
An annual bonus declared by the insurer and added permanently to the sum assured of a participating policy. Expressed as a rate per ₦1,000 sum assured per year.
Interest or usury; the Islamic prohibition on earning or paying interest, making conventional insurance investment Shari’ah-impermissible.
The possibility that an unfavourable event will occur, resulting in financial loss.
The level and types of risk an insurer is willing to accept in pursuit of its strategic objectives.
The Board-approved document articulating the insurer’s risk appetite across all material risk categories.
The categorisation of an applicant’s risk level (standard, substandard, declined) based on the underwriting assessment.
The Board committee overseeing the ERM framework, risk appetite, and ORSA.
The rate used to discount future profits in embedded value calculations, reflecting the required return on the capital supporting the life business.
A visual tool displaying risks by their likelihood and potential impact, enabling prioritisation of risk management attention.
A specific quantitative boundary on an individual risk within the overall risk appetite (e.g., maximum single-name credit exposure).
The individual responsible for managing a specific risk within the ERM framework.
The fundamental insurance mechanism: many policyholders contribute premiums to a common fund from which the losses of the few are paid.
The comprehensive record of all identified material risks, their assessments, owners, and mitigation actions.
The acceptable degree of variation around the risk appetite level; the boundary between outcomes that trigger management action and those that do not.
A capital requirement framework that links the minimum capital the insurer must hold to its specific risk profile, replacing the traditional fixed-percentage solvency margin.

Software mimicking human actions in digital systems to automate high-volume, rule-based tasks without changing the underlying systems; valuable for premium reconciliation, regulatory return preparation, and commission calculation.
Software robots that automate repetitive rule-based processes such as data entry, report generation, and premium reconciliation.
The managed wind-down of an insurer’s portfolio of obligations after it has ceased writing new business.
A cultural pathology in which agents are incentivised to maximise sales volume regardless of product suitability for the buyer; a primary target of NIIRA 2025’s consumer protection provisions.
NAICOM’s controlled environment for testing innovative insurance models under supervision before full licensing.
The evaluation of the insurer’s financial position under defined hypothetical scenarios; input to the ORSA.
The part of the policy document setting out the specific details of the coverage (insured name, sum assured, premium, effective date).
The discipline of optimising website content and structure so that relevant pages rank prominently in search engine results, generating organic (unpaid) traffic from high-intent users.
A web or app interface enabling policyholders to manage their policy without contacting the insurer: premium payment, document download, contact updates, and claims initiation.
A direct fee charged by the broker to the client for professional advisory services, in addition to or instead of brokerage commission.
A commitment by the insurer to deliver a defined standard of service within a defined timeframe. SLAs convert subjective service quality into measurable, manageable performance targets.
The agreed payment resolving a claim between the insurer and the claimant.
The magnitude of a single loss event; one of the two components of the expected loss (frequency × severity).
Islamic law derived from the Qur’an, Sunnah, scholarly consensus, and analogical reasoning.
The independent body of Islamic scholars certifying the Shari’ah compliance of a Takaful operator’s products, investments, and operations.
A policy funded by a single lump-sum premium paid at inception, rather than periodic premiums.
The document summarising the key terms of a facultative reinsurance placement, initialled by each reinsurer to indicate their acceptance of a line.
A self-executing programme on a blockchain that automatically implements agreement terms when predefined conditions are met.

The European Union’s comprehensive risk-based insurance regulatory framework, effective January 2016, structured around three pillars (quantitative capital requirements, governance and risk management, reporting and disclosure). Serves as the primary international benchmark for NIIRA 2025’s RBC framework.
The excess of an insurer’s assets over its liabilities; the financial buffer protecting policyholders.
The insurer’s actual capital as a percentage of the required minimum capital under the applicable solvency framework.
The number of direct reports managed by a single manager.

Personal data in sensitive categories requiring heightened protection: health data, biometric data, genetic data, racial or ethnic origin, political opinions, religious beliefs, sexual orientation, and criminal record data.
The unit within the Claims department responsible for investigating claims presenting fraud indicators.
A dedicated team within the claims function responsible for investigating claims where fraud indicators are present. The SIU operates independently of the claims approval function.
NDPC-approved contractual terms providing adequate safeguards for cross-border data transfers where no adequacy decision exists.
A policyholder whose risk profile falls within the normal parameters for standard premium rates; neither a substandard risk nor a preferred risk.
The Fellow of a recognised actuarial institute responsible for certifying the annual actuarial investigation, with a direct reporting line to the Board under NIIRA 2025.

The separate fund maintained by a life insurer into which all life insurance premiums and investment income are paid, held in trust for life policyholders and segregated from non-life and shareholder funds.
The annual regulatory filing submitted by a licensed insurer to NAICOM, including financial statements, actuarial report, and market conduct data.

A non-proportional reinsurance arrangement that limits the cedant’s aggregate claims experience in a year to a defined percentage of premium income. The reinsurer pays the excess above the attachment point.
Automated policy issuance without human underwriter review, applicable to low-risk applications that satisfy all automated triage criteria.
The risk that the insurer’s strategy is fundamentally flawed or that execution is so poor that strategic objectives are not achieved.

The set of deliberate choices an organisation makes about which customers to serve, which products to offer, which distribution channels to invest in, and which capabilities to build, creating a distinctive and defensible competitive position.
The evaluation of an insurer’s financial resilience by applying severe but plausible adverse scenarios to its balance sheet and income statement.
Formal, documented learning activities that generate CIIN CPD credit hours.
Employer-granted time for examination preparation; best practice for insurers sponsoring CIIN qualifications.

The right of the insurer, after paying a claim, to take over the insured’s legal rights to pursue recovery from third parties responsible for the loss. Limited relevance in life insurance but applicable in some accident and liability contexts.
An applicant whose risk profile is worse than the standard (e.g., due to health conditions or hazardous occupation) and who is accepted at a higher premium or with exclusions.
The systematic identification and development of candidates for critical roles.
The arrangement for managing RSA balances and pension benefits in the event of the RSA holder’s death before retirement.

A policy exclusion that limits the insurer’s liability to a return of premiums where death by suicide occurs within the first 12 to 24 months of the policy. After the exclusion period, the full sum assured is payable.
The requirement under NIIRA 2025 that the product or advice provided must be genuinely appropriate for the client’s specific circumstances, needs, and risk tolerance.

A documented assessment of a customer’s needs, financial circumstances, and risk tolerance conducted before recommending an insurance product, to establish that the recommended product is genuinely suitable for the customer.
An Islamic bond structured around asset-backed returns rather than interest payments; a key Shari’ah-compliant investment instrument for Takaful funds.
The defined benefit amount payable under a life insurance policy on occurrence of the covered event.
The net amount at risk to the insurer: the difference between the sum assured and the policy reserve.
An ML approach trained on labelled data (examples with known correct answers), used for predictive tasks with defined outcomes: fraud detection, lapse prediction, automated underwriting.
NAICOM’s ongoing monitoring of licensed insurers’ financial soundness, governance, and market conduct.
A graduated framework of NAICOM supervisory actions keyed to defined solvency ratio bands, from enhanced monitoring at 110–129% through NAICOM taking operational control below 80%.
A proportional treaty under which the cedant retains a defined line (fixed sum) and cedes the surplus above the retained line.
The voluntary termination of a life insurance policy by the policyholder before maturity, typically in exchange for the surrender value.
The amount payable to the policyholder on voluntary termination of a life insurance policy before its maturity or expiry date.

A periodic payment made under a money-back plan to a policyholder who is alive on a defined anniversary date during the policy term. Survival benefits are a scheduled contractual entitlement, not discretionary.
The minimum period the insured must survive after a critical illness diagnosis before the CI benefit is payable.
The minimum period (typically 14–30 days) a policyholder must survive after the diagnosis of a critical illness before the CI benefit becomes payable.
A formal report filed by the MLRO with the NFIU where the insurer has reason to suspect that a transaction involves the proceeds of crime or is connected to terrorist financing.

Insurance products designed to create insurance value while advancing environmental or social objectives: parametric agricultural coverage, renewable energy business insurance, financial inclusion life products, and wellness-incentivised group health.
The insurance industry’s most authoritative global research series, published by Swiss Re Institute, providing country-level market data, emerging risk analysis, and distribution innovation research.
The alignment of textbook content to CIIN examination syllabus topics; this glossary chapter provides a reference index for examination preparation.
An Islamic donation or charitable contribution; Takaful participants make Tabaru’ contributions to the mutual fund rather than paying premiums for a contractual benefit.
Islamic insurance based on mutual contribution, shared risk, and Shari’ah-compliant investment.
A ring-fenced Takaful operation within a conventional insurer’s corporate structure, with strict fund separation and its own SSB.

Task Force on Climate-related Financial Disclosures: an international framework for reporting climate-related risks and opportunities, whose recommendations are increasingly reflected in financial sector regulation.

The income statement presentation of the insurer’s insurance underwriting result (premium income less claims incurred, reserve changes, and distribution expenses) before investment income is included.
The insurer’s reinsurance result: premiums ceded minus claims recovered.
The liabilities of an insurer relating to its insurance contracts, including the policy reserve, claims reserves, and other actuarial provisions.

A classification of an insurer’s current technology capability level, used to sequence investment priorities from foundational (PAS, premium reconciliation) through to differentiating (AI, embedded distribution).

The measurable return on a technology investment, expressed through specific operational metrics: cycle time reduction, cost saving, compliance rate improvement, or revenue growth attributable to the investment.
A structured health disclosure interview conducted by a trained specialist by telephone, replacing or supplementing the written health declaration section of the proposal form.
Technology that collects real-time data on the behaviour of an insured asset (vehicle, person) for pricing and monitoring.
A short-term insurance coverage document issued while the formal underwriting and policy issuance process is completed, confirming that the risk is covered for a defined period.
The defined period during which an insurance policy provides coverage.
Pure life insurance providing a death benefit only if the insured dies within the defined term; no maturity benefit on survival.
A discretionary additional bonus paid at the point of claim (death or maturity), over and above accumulated reversionary bonuses. Not guaranteed.
An external company that manages claims on behalf of an insurer, commonly used in group health insurance.
The minimum mandatory motor insurance under the Motor Vehicles (Third Party Insurance) Act.
The governance model in which operational management (1st line) owns risk; Risk and Compliance (2nd line) designs the framework; Internal Audit (3rd line) provides independent assurance.

A risk governance model assigning risk management responsibilities to: the first line (business functions that own and manage risks); the second line (CRO and risk/compliance functions that oversee and challenge); and the third line (internal audit that provides independent assurance).
An agent who sells the products of a single insurer only, as opposed to an independent or multi-insurer agent.
The principle that senior leadership behaviour is the most powerful determinant of organisational culture.
A market sizing approach that starts from total population or economic aggregates and progressively narrows to the addressable and realistically acquirable market.

A condition in which the policyholder is, due to illness or injury, permanently and totally unable to engage in any occupation for which they are reasonably qualified, or their own specific occupation, depending on the policy definition.
The full five-year cost of a PAS, including licence fees, implementation, customisation, training, support, and upgrade costs; the correct basis for PAS financial evaluation.
The historical dataset used to train an ML model, containing input features and labelled outcomes; the primary determinant of model quality.

The risk of financial loss arising from the economic and policy adjustments required to transition to a lower-carbon economy, including carbon pricing, stranded fossil fuel assets, and technological disruption.
Pension benefit payable to employees with service under pre-CPS DB schemes at the time of the 2004 transition.
A short-term government debt instrument with maturity of one year or less; the primary money market instrument for Nigerian insurers.
The NIIRA 2025 regulatory principle requiring insurers to ensure their products, distribution, servicing, and claims management genuinely deliver fair outcomes to policyholders.
A reinsurance agreement covering a defined class of business automatically, without requiring case-by-case cession.

A standing reinsurance agreement covering all risks of a defined class automatically, without individual case negotiation. Every qualifying risk is automatically ceded and accepted under the treaty terms.
A legal arrangement in which assets are held by a trustee for the benefit of beneficiaries; used in life insurance for estate planning.
The deeply embedded consumer scepticism about insurance companies in Nigeria, rooted in historical claims payment failures and the perception that insurers will find reasons not to pay valid claims.
Latin for ‘utmost good faith’. The legal doctrine requiring both parties to an insurance contract to disclose all material information fully and honestly.
Life assurance benefit proceeds that the insurer is unable to pay because the policyholder or beneficiary cannot be located after documented tracing efforts.
A NAICOM-administered central repository to which life insurers must remit unclaimed benefit proceeds that remain outstanding after the prescribed statutory period.
The process of assessing a proposed risk and deciding whether to accept it and at what premium and terms.
The portion of written premium relating to future coverage periods; must be ceded to reinsurers in proportion to the cession ratio.
A manager responsible for a team of tied agents within the insurer’s field sales structure.
A supervisory role in the retail agency hierarchy who recruits, trains, and supervises a team of 8–15 agents and earns an overrider commission on the team’s production.
A standalone insurance company licensed specifically under NAICOM’s Microinsurance Guidelines to write only microinsurance products for the low-income market.
An insurance product combining life coverage with investment in market-linked unit trust funds.
A flexible life insurance product allowing the policyholder to vary the premium and the sum assured within defined limits.
The increase or decrease in the market value of an investment that has not yet been converted to cash through a sale.
Increasing the coverage amount or adding riders to an existing policy, expanding the policyholder’s protection and the insurer’s premium income from the existing relationship.
A structured testing programme conducted by business users (not IT staff) to verify that every material business scenario works correctly in the new PAS before go-live.
Unstructured Supplementary Service Data; a mobile communication protocol enabling insurance services without internet access.

A telecommunications protocol enabling interactive mobile sessions using simple numeric menus, accessible from any mobile phone without internet connectivity. Used for insurance distribution, premium payment, and claims notification.
The process of enrolling in an insurance product using the USSD mobile telephone protocol, which works on any mobile phone without internet connectivity, through sequential text menus.
Insurance distribution through Unstructured Supplementary Service Data (USSD) codes on mobile phones, enabling policy purchase without internet access.
The obligation on both the insurer and the policyholder to act honestly and disclose all relevant information; the foundation of the insurance contract.
The set of actuarial assumptions (mortality table, interest rate, lapse rate, expense assumptions) used to calculate policy reserves in the annual actuarial valuation.
The present value of future after-tax shareholder profits expected from the existing in-force policy portfolio.

The design principle that a microinsurance product’s benefit must be clearly understandable to the target customer in concrete, tangible terms relevant to their own life, not in actuarial or technical terms.

The IFRS 17 measurement model for direct participating contracts where policyholders share in the returns of a clearly identified pool of underlying items. CSM adjusts for changes in the fair value of the underlying items.
The operational and strategic risk arising from excessive dependency on a single technology vendor across multiple critical systems.
The process by which an employee’s right to employer pension contributions or deferred compensation becomes unconditional.
An AI-powered digital assistant that performs agent-like functions (lead qualification, needs analysis, product recommendation) without a human agent.
A policy that is treated as never having existed, typically because of a material misrepresentation or non-disclosure by the proposer.
A policy that is valid unless and until the insurer exercises its right to avoid it, typically due to non-disclosure discovered after the policy was issued.
An above-minimum, tax-deductible RSA contribution available to CPS members and the self-employed.
An RSA opened specifically for voluntary contributions by individuals outside mandatory CPS coverage.

A customer who, due to personal circumstances (bereavement, illness, low literacy, financial distress, advanced age), is at greater risk of harm from the insurer’s actions or inactions than a typical customer.
A defined period after policy inception during which certain benefits are not payable; used to manage adverse selection particularly in health insurance.
A defined period after enrolment during which certain benefits (particularly for pre-existing conditions or maternity) are not payable.

An add-on to an insurance policy that waives all future premiums if the policyholder becomes totally and permanently disabled, while the policy continues to maturity at the original projected benefit.
An Islamic agency contract in which one party acts as agent for another for a defined fee; the dominant Takaful operating model in Nigeria.
An Islamic endowment dedicated to a charitable purpose; used as a Takaful fund structure in the Waqf model.
A statement of fact in an insurance contract that must be strictly true; breach of warranty entitles the insurer to repudiate the contract, regardless of whether the breach is material to the loss.
A term in an insurance contract that must be strictly true; a strict condition of coverage.
The enterprise-grade WhatsApp integration enabling insurers to send automated messages, receive inbound queries, and build chatbot interactions at scale through a verified business number.

The reporting by an insider of suspected wrongdoing, illegal activity, or regulatory non-compliance. NIIRA 2025 requires a formal whistleblowing framework including anonymous reporting channels and a non-retaliation guarantee.
Life insurance providing permanent death cover with no fixed maturity date, building a cash value over time.
The placement of risks with insurers on behalf of retail brokers rather than ultimate clients. The wholesale broker provides specialist market access or international placement capability.
See Participating Policy.
Software-driven management of a business process, in which each step is triggered automatically when the preceding step is completed, tracked against deadlines, and escalated if overdue.
A distribution strategy in which insurers or agents access an employer’s workforce to sell insurance products, typically using payroll deductions for premium collection.
A group life reinsurance structure under which the cedant retains the first defined amount of each individual claim and cedes the excess.

Nigeria’s demographic characteristic of a very young population (median age approximately 18 years) representing a major long-term opportunity for insurance market expansion as this cohort moves through the peak insurance-buying life stages over the next two decades.
